meta.title: Suntiq GTM Research — Analysis and Initial Direction
meta.description: An evidence-backed briefing on what the marine fleet market understands, where the white space may be, what breaks the thesis, and what must be proven next.

props.title: Protect the promised trip, not the dashboard.
props.subtitle: The initial wedge is condition-aware trip fulfillment and exception ownership. It remains a hypothesis.
props.meta: 30 competitor sites · 12 transcripts · 100 curated reviews · 50 Reddit threads · 50 X posts

props.content: Boat-club customers are not buying access to inventory. They are buying a dependable boating day without ownership work. The market already has booking systems, maintenance tools, monitoring products, and local operating expertise. The unresolved question is whether a repeated, costly decision gap remains between a boat's condition, the trips that depend on it, and the person who must act before the promise fails.

props.title: Run diagnosis before product
props.content: Do not lead with hardware, telemetry, AI, a fleet dashboard, or a claim that Suntiq is the missing system. Reconstruct recent failed departures, test whether the configured incumbent stack and an ordinary process fix can solve the material causes, and stop if they can.
props.next: Only accounts with a repeated preventable loss pool and an unresolved decision gap advance to a read-only shadow test.

props.label: Evidence boundary
props.title: The thesis survives model pressure; it has not survived the market yet
What the evidence can establish
props.content:
The external corpus supports a real problem class: recurring failures involving availability, condition, preparation, recovery, and communication. It also shows crowded booking, administration, maintenance, and monitoring categories.

Synthetic UX, CDO, and Tribunal work improved the study design and attacked the candidate wedge. It does not establish problem prevalence inside one operator ICP, buyer authority, willingness to pay, product causality, or repeatable economics.

The exact current stage is **solution validation in progress**. Product validation is not auditable and commercial validation is absent.

props.title: Free pilots are not commercial proof
props.content: Interest in a complimentary pilot shows willingness to explore an approach. It does not show willingness to pay. No named executed agreement, activation, repeated workflow, measured outcome, payment, renewal, or expansion is portable in the research package.

props.label: Four independent passes
props.title: The research was not collapsed into one generic market summary
props.subtitle: Each pass queried the Lev/QMD corpus independently, then checked claims against raw ledgers and source artifacts.

props.label: Pass 1
props.title: Implicit truths
props.content: What successful operators behave as though they know, even when customers do not say it directly: availability is an operating state, recovery is part of the product, local execution defines trust, and data matters only when it changes a staff decision.

props.label: Pass 2
props.title: Assumptions and falsifiers
props.content: Eight market assumptions were translated into observable failure conditions. The strongest kill test is simple: if the configured incumbent stack or a cheap process change answers the real operating decision, Suntiq should stop.

props.label: Pass 3
props.title: Consensus, blind spots, white space
props.content: The crowded centers are booking and administration on one side, monitoring and maintenance on the other. The candidate white space is not another center; it is the exception loop joining condition, affected trip, owner, recovery, and outcome.

props.title: Investor attack
props.content: The thesis still breaks on ICP concentration, willingness to pay, operator adoption, hardware and support burden, defensibility, channel quality, founder-network bias, and untested unit economics.

props.title: What successful players appear to understand
props.content:
## Seven implicit truths

1. Customers buy a dependable boating day, not access to a boat.
2. Availability is a condition state, not a calendar state.
3. Exception recovery is the product at the moment trust is decided.
4. A network brand is only as strong as local operating consistency.
5. Peak scarcity is structural; honest management beats impossible guarantees.
6. Data creates value only when it changes the next staff action.
7. Usage is the customer-health signal; operating leverage is the business prize.

The important consequence is that alert volume, dashboard engagement, and hardware deployment are weak north stars. The operating unit to protect is the fulfilled, safe boat-day.

props.label: Falsification
props.title: The market thesis earns the right to continue only by surviving these tests

rows.assumption: Members buy relief from ownership work
rows.why: Club positioning repeatedly sells maintenance-free access and service.
rows.wrong: Price, social identity, or raw access dominates reliability.
rows.test: Rank the last five value moments and failure moments without showing product language.

rows.assumption: Availability is more than a reservation screen
rows.why: Reviews connect confirmed access to readiness, cleanliness, delay, and substitution.
rows.wrong: Most failed trips are fixed capacity, weather, policy, or staffing.
rows.test: Reconstruct the last five delayed, substituted, or canceled departures.

rows.assumption: Fragmented tools create a costly decision gap
rows.why: Booking, maintenance, monitoring, dock work, and communication live in separate systems.
rows.wrong: Operators already answer the readiness questions quickly from one trusted workflow.
rows.test: Ten configured-stack drills; stop if five answer all five questions in under two minutes.

rows.why: Monitoring vendors sell visibility; customer failures often surface too late.
rows.wrong: Signals are noisy, unactionable, or earlier than staff can use.
rows.test: Read-only shadow timestamps plus a changed-decision log and comparator.

rows.assumption: The operator will pay for the joined workflow
rows.why: Prevented lost trips and coordination time could have economic value.
rows.wrong: The budget is absent, the value unit is wrong, or a service/process fix is cheaper.
rows.test: Dated intended-price rollout decisions and fully loaded economics.

props.label: Market map
props.title: The candidate is a seam between crowded categories

props.label: Consensus
props.title: Booking, administration, maintenance, monitoring
props.content: Successful vendors organize inventory, reservations, payments, maintenance work, sensor data, and local operations. They correctly assume that recurring participation and operating leverage matter more than one-time unit sales.

props.title: Candidate white space
props.content: Connect one real operating exception across condition evidence, affected bookings, accountable owner, deadline, repair or substitution, member recovery, and measured outcome—without replacing the systems already in place.

props.label: Operating logic
props.title: The product must earn its way into the workflow
props.subtitle: Every branch has a stop rule. Hardware appears only after current data and ordinary process improvements fail.

props.caption: The diagnostic sequence preserves incumbent tools as authoritative and prevents free hardware from masquerading as validation.

props.title: Bounded thesis
props.claim: Condition-aware trip fulfillment is the best current wedge, not an established market category.
props.evidence: Independent corpus passes converge on availability as an operating outcome, fragmented failure recovery, and data-to-action as the value boundary. All seven complete Tribunal judgments ranked this wedge first.
props.source: Implicit truths, consensus/white-space analysis, and Tribunal report
props.limitation: Only seven of twenty-two Tribunal cells completed, from one provider family. No real operator cohort has yet established prevalence, causal impact, or willingness to pay.

props.label: Evidence ladder
props.title: The exact gates between a thesis and product-market fit

rows.pass: 15–20 same-ICP conversations; 12 rank one failure top-three; 8 quantify cost and buyer.
rows.current: Corpus shows a real problem class, not same-ICP prevalence.

rows.pass: More than 5 of 10 cannot answer five readiness questions in one trusted workflow under two minutes.
At least 3 of 5 pilots repeat signal → owner → action → closure without founder prompting.
rows.current: No auditable activation or repeated workflow.

rows.pass: At least 3 of 5 hit a signed downtime, fulfilled-trip, or labor threshold against a verified baseline.
At least 3 of 5 sign dated intended-price rollouts with no more than 20% concession.
rows.current: Pilots are free; no paid commitments.

rows.pass: At least 65% gross margin, at most 12-month CAC payback, and two non-founder-network wins.

props.label: Economics
props.title: The free pilot is an experiment, not the offer

props.label: Free R&D pilot
props.title: Measure every cost the zero-dollar price hides
props.content: Hardware, provisioning, connectivity, installation labor, travel, integration, support, revisits, replacements, founder intervention, and sales effort must be logged. Pilot price is fixed at $0; blanks must remain unknown rather than becoming zero.

props.title: Commercial decision
props.content: Before the free period ends, every pilot needs a dated decision at the intended price. Commercial validation requires at least three signed rollouts from five pilots, acceptable delivery margin, and a start within sixty days.

props.label: Message candidate
props.title: Speak like the calm fleet operator in the room
props.subtitle: This is research language for testing, not an approved brand standard.

props.title: Candidate message
props.content:
## One-liner

Suntiq helps multi-location boat operators turn vessel condition into owned action for the trips that need attention.

## Operator narrative

A reservation can look confirmed while the boat is not actually ready. The condition may live in one system, the booking in another, and the response in calls and texts. Suntiq is designed to identify the affected trip, show the evidence, assign one owner, and record the recovery while the tools and local judgment already in place remain authoritative.

props.title: Do not say yet
props.content: Predictive maintenance, proven ROI, validated demand, commercial traction, increased availability, market-leading AI, a single pane of glass, or guaranteed outcomes. Promote only language operators recognize without founder explanation.

props.label: Next evidence cycle
props.title: Four moves remain between research and a real GTM motion
Make pilots auditable
props.content: Map each reported pilot to a named CRM opportunity, executed agreement state, owner, baseline, success metric, permissions, deployment count, and decision date.

props.title: Run 15–20 conversations
props.content: Start with the last five failed departures. Capture problem ranking, loss, buyer, counterexamples, and operator-native language before showing Suntiq.

props.title: Run five measured pilots
props.content: Compare current process, the cheapest incumbent improvement, read-only Suntiq, and hardware only where it adds independent signal.

props.title: Get a real-price decision
props.content: Require a dated yes or no from every pilot. Three of five intended-price rollouts are the commercial gate; continued free use is not.
